findings.issue: The two adapters treat empty slices differently. factStoreCloneBlocks (and the Display clone at line 100) use append(nil, in...), which turns an empty non-nil slice into nil. The SQLite adapter round-trips [] as an empty non-nil slice. So the memory adapter hands back nil blocks for a stored empty set, while factStoreCloneFacts (make) keeps them non-nil. TestFactStoreReplacesPreviousSet works around this with len(b) != 0 instead of DeepEqual. That makes 'nothing stored' (nil, nil, nil) look the same as 'stored an empty set' in memory but not in SQLite.
findings.fix: Clone with make+copy (or slices.Clone) in both helpers so nil stays nil and empty stays empty. Then add a both-adapter subtest that stores empty facts and blocks and compares the result with reflect.DeepEqual.

findings.issue: TestFactStoreMemoryReturnsCopies throws away the errors from newFactStore and both LatestFacts calls (s, _ := ...; got, _, _ := ...). If either call failed, the test would panic on got[0] instead of reporting a clear failure. The other tests in the file do check every error.
findings.fix: Check each error with t.Fatalf, as the sibling tests do.

findings.issue: Possible Primitive Obsession: the memory key is a bare [3]string built in two places, so the reader has to remember the order tenant/actor/section.
findings.fix: Use a small struct key { tenant, actor, sectionID string } built by one helper that calls identity.StorageTenant.
